text: Nightfarers take shelter in the Sacred Tree area during the third day before facing the Night Lord, since the land will fall if a third night passes.
The Night Farers arrived in Limveld at different times or in clusters rather than all at once, with some more experienced and adapted to the world than others.
Some item locations in Limveld are only populated during the early hours of the first night and disappear by the second night, implying their origin forces are tied to the world's most dormant state.
Certain NPC encounters in Limveld are only accessible during the transition between the second and third nights, when normally fixed world boundaries become temporarily permeable.
The transition from the second to third night features a brief, complete silence in the game's ambient soundscape before the third night's sounds begin.
The Three Nights structure represents not just a gameplay loop but an escalating cosmological process that Limveld is continuously undergoing since its catastrophe began.

During the first night, Limveld is in its most restrained state: Night Lord forces are present but not fully manifest, ruins remain navigable, enemies fight in comprehensible ways, and sites of grace remain stable, providing reliable rest.
The second night is the most unstable part of the cycle, a transitional state where the world is neither fully its old self nor fully its new post-catastrophe nature.
Enemies encountered in the second night are versions of first-night enemies that more fully express the forces animating them, rather than the preserved forms of the old civilization.
The third night is the full revelation and culmination of the escalation that began in the first two nights.
After each expedition, Limveld's physical state resets to its first-night conditions.
The position of the world within each night (time of day) correlates with changing dangers and accessibility, requiring players to learn to read these shifts.
The sites of grace in Limveld, even flickering or compromised ones, are remnants of a relationship between the world and divine forces that the catastrophe damaged but could not fully sever.
Unlike the Iron Menial, the Nightfarers have forgotten much of their past, with memories dissipating the longer they fight the Night.
Throughout the game, Nightfarers' memories gradually return, allowing players to witness flashbacks of their past.
The Iron Menial sends Wilder to retrieve a wet stone from the mines of Limveld, guarded by a crystallian.
After defeating the first boss, Wilder can obtain a Pocket Watch, which is needed to unlock the Duchess as a playable Nightfarer.
The Round Table Hold will cease to exist once the Night Lord is defeated, and since the Duchess is tied to the Round Table's existence, she will disappear along with it.
A note from the Iron Menial explains that an object blessed by the Priestess could travel beyond the Round Table Hold to connect with Wilder before his death, functioning as a fetish.
The Iron Menial instructs the Nightfarers to discard the cursed charms given by the merchant.
'Condemned' are corrupted Nightfarers from other failed timelines/worlds who succumbed to the Night and can be found at special map locations marked with a green and blue circle.
According to the Duchess, Condemned beings can multiply and spread their corruption from world to world.

The Revenant is the only Nightfarer able to summon allies into battle—Helen, Frederick, and Sebastian—using her lyre; her codex describes them as a page, cook, and butler respectively, possibly tied to Northern Croft's noble status.
Activating the Revenant's ultimate ability reveals a skull visible behind her facial frame.

The Executor's ultimate transforms him into a beast form, reflecting a Crucible aspect called 'Beast,' reminiscent of the massive creature in the Specimen Storehouse beneath the Shadow of the Erdtree region.
The Round Table identifies six other Night Lord traces; defeating these beasts yields Essence of Night, and collecting four reveals the true Night Lord.
